KANO (PSI 9.8): Approved N144.01bn for capital infrastructure projects, including major urban road dualization and health upgrades, while transmitting a N1.201T supplementary budget.
OGUN (PSI 9.7): Signed landmark MoUs with DP World in Paris for the construction of the $7bn Gateway Deep Sea Port and 10,000-hectare Blue Marine Special Economic Zone.
ZAMFARA (PSI 9.6): Showcased state gold, lithium, and copper potential to US investors at UNGA 81 while reiterating zero tolerance for gender-based violence.
JIGAWA (PSI 9.5): Launched the AgriConnect Compact with 400 tractors across 60 mechanization centers and engaged the Forum of Jigawa Academics on evidence-based policymaking.
KATSINA (PSI 9.4): Commissioned a solar-powered borehole and renovated secondary school executed by the Nigerian Navy in Gidan Mutum Daya while highlighting N36.8bn security investments.
LAGOS (PSI 9.3): Pitched Lagos as Africa's business gateway at UNGA 81 in New York, provided N100k grants to 200 PWDs, and unveiled a FIFA-standard natural grass pitch at Teslim Balogun Stadium.
CROSS RIVER (PSI 9.2): Surpassed 2026 electricity expansion targets by 5%, deployed GIS digital tracking for livestock management, and inaugurated a probe into Giant Cement mining claims.
EDO (PSI 9.1): Pledged N100m for Uwelu Spare Parts Market traders, enrolled 1,000 youths in LIFE-ND agribusiness, and commissioned Yongxing Steel's Catholic Charity Home.
BORNO (PSI 9.0): Received the 2026 Quintessence Top Leadership Award in New Jersey, dedicating the honor to Borno's resilient citizens while urging diaspora investment back home.
ENUGU (PSI 8.9): Challenged over 300 media editors at ANEC to ground reporting in evidence and truth, receiving the Nigerian Guild of Editors Good Governance Plaque.
ONDO (PSI 8.8): Approved upward reviews for car, housing, and duty tour allowances while injecting N500m additional seed funding into worker loan schemes.
AKWA IBOM (PSI 8.7): Commissioned the Uruan Youth Centre for practical skills, engaged PHED management on electricity market frameworks, and held 2nd memorial for late First Lady.
FCT ABUJA (PSI 8.6): Inspected Phase II dualization of Kuje-Gwagwalada road, guaranteeing full funding to Gilmor Engineering for December completion and announcing FCT campaign plans.
OSUN (PSI 8.5): Hosted Alive & Kicking investors in London to establish a football manufacturing factory in the Osun Free Trade Zone and launch a talent academy.
TARABA (PSI 8.4): Inspected ongoing works at TAARDS agricultural facility, two secondary schools, and Specialist Hospital, while commiserating with Mambilla Royal Family.
NASARAWA (PSI 8.3): Commissioned the 5.2km Damishi Luka Akwanga Bypass, along with local township roads in Wamba and Nasarawa Eggon, and inspected DASH specialist hospital works.
KEBBI (PSI 8.2): Donated 500 bags of rice to Sakaba IDPs via Nasara Foundation while the NUT National President hailed Governor Idris as a pride to Nigerian teachers.
ABIA (PSI 8.1): Unveiled modernized solarized Cottage Hospital Umuihie and directed security agencies during State Security Council to ensure unhindered campaign access for all parties.
PLATEAU (PSI 8.0): Distributed toilet building materials to 170 households in Langtang North under SURWASH while Transport Ministry addressed VIO conduct following recent officer assaults.
NIGER (PSI 7.8): Approved the implementation of tax-free Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and CONTTA for IBBU Lapai and AKUM Minna staff effective October 2026.
DELTA (PSI 7.7): Constituted an 8-member administrative panel into Deputy Director Adeda Ekwevugbe's death, prompting Organised Labour to direct civil servants to resume duties.
RIVERS (PSI 7.6): Represented by Deputy Governor, urged traditional rulers to preserve cultural heritage at King Jaja VI coronation, attended by former President Goodluck Jonathan.
EBONYI (PSI 7.5): Assured OHANIVO bloc leaders of accelerated development and Oshiri-Ugwulangwu road completion while urging political support for President Tinubu and 2027 reelection.
ADAMAWA (PSI 7.4): Effected Ministry of Energy administrative transition to Hon. Bramsy Caleb and conducted public sanitation compliance monitoring across Yola North and South.
GOMBE (PSI 7.2): Ranked 3rd nationwide and 1st in the North-East by NBS/TheCableIndex after generating N8.92bn in internal revenues from local government areas in 2025.
KADUNA (PSI 7.0): Announced application exercise for National Diploma in Nursing across Tudun Wada, Kafanchan, and Pambegua campuses for candidates scoring 150+ in JAMB.
